chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from al-Fadl ibn Yasar, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a man who slaughtered an animal, but the knife preceded (the cut) and severed it, so he said: 'It is a valid slaughter, it is alive, and there is no harm in eating it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on an animal if the knife cuts through it before the soul departs during slaughter?
ai.summary: In this narration from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that if the knife severs the throat before the soul fully departs, the animal is considered 'alive' (hiyyah) and its slaughter valid (dhakah), rendering it permissible to eat. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that the act of slaughter is complete once the major vessels are cut, even if the animal is still twitching or conscious, distinguishing it from animals that die from the cut alone without proper slaughter rites. The hadith underscores the importance of intention and the physical act of cutting in determining the status of the meat as halal.
